text.en: In Basketball, Cricket, Football, Hockey, and Volleyball, no single player wins alone. Passing, defending, and trusting teammates turn individual skills into team victory.

Team games require shared goals, communication, decision-making, and cooperation. Chapter 6 covers Basketball, Cricket, Football, Field Hockey, and Volleyball.
Basketball is played by 5 players per team on court; games start with a jump ball, field goals score 2 or 3 points, free throws score 1 point, and 5 personal fouls disqualify a player.
Cricket is played between two teams of 11 players (plus a 12th man substitute fielder) on an oval field with a central pitch; runs are scored by running or hitting boundaries (4 or 6).
Football (soccer) is played in two 45-minute halves on a rectangular pitch (goalposts 7.32 m wide × 2.44 m high); throw-ins use both hands from behind and over the head.
Field Hockey is played on a 91.40 m × 55 m field using curved sticks; defenders must stay 5 m away on free hits, and fouls inside the shooting circle can earn a penalty corner.
Volleyball has 6 playing players per team (12 total) separated by a net (2.43 m men, 2.24 m women); each team may touch the ball up to 3 times before sending it over.
Team games build communication, trust, and joint problem-solving.
Basketball: 5 players on court, 2- or 3-point shots, 1-point free throws, and man-to-man or zone defence.
Cricket: 11 players per side, boundaries of 4 and 6 runs, and modes of dismissal like bowled, LBW, and stumped.
Football: two 45-minute halves, 7.32 m × 2.44 m goalposts, and two-handed overhead throw-ins.
Field Hockey: 91.40 m × 55 m field, 14.63 m shooting circle, and penalty corners.
Volleyball: 6 players on court, net height 2.43 m (men) / 2.24 m (women), max 3 team touches.

problem.en: In Volleyball, Player A passes the ball to Player B, who sets it to Player C, who spikes it over the net. Is this legal?

why.en: Volleyball allows up to three consecutive contacts per team.

text.en: Check if any single player touched it twice in a row: No.

why.en: A player cannot make two consecutive contacts (except after a block). So it is completely legal.

prompt.en: Summarise the key team size and scoring/playing rules for any three sports in Chapter 6.

requiredIdeas.en: Basketball has 5 players on court with 2/3-point baskets and 1-point free throws
Cricket has 11 players per team with 4/6 boundaries; Football has two 45-minute halves
Volleyball has 6 players on court and allows 3 team contacts

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking a Volleyball player can touch the ball twice consecutively or catch and throw it

points.en: Basketball: 5 players on court, jump ball start, 5-foul limit, 1/2/3-point scoring.
Cricket: 11 players + 12th man fielder, ICC governance, batting/bowling/fielding.
Football: 90 minutes (two 45-min halves), 7.32 m × 2.44 m goal, overhead throw-in.
Field Hockey (91.40×55 m) and Volleyball (6 players, max 3 touches) require tight teamwork.
